correctness.rationale: Renewal on independent reset attempts gives M(b)=(1-H(b))/(rH(b)) with H=K_kappa*mu, kappa=sqrt(r/D). On the right tail of compactly supported mu, H=C exp(-kappa b), fixing kappa by log M slope. F(s)=integral(1+sM)^-1 db is continuous strictly decreasing from infinity to zero and equals 2/kappa only at physical s=r; then distributional Helmholtz inversion recovers arbitrary atomic/continuous mu and D=r/kappa^2. On an interval, annihilating the exponential-kernel convolution forces zero signed measure internally and two weighted external masses zero. Fourier multiplier 2kappa/(kappa^2+xi^2) makes smooth density oscillations decay at exact n^-2 while TV tends to epsilon/pi. Independent direct 1-vs-2-atom equivalence check confirms the local ambiguity example.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge novelty rests in simultaneous identification of unknown r, D and compactly supported reset law from one spatial target scan at fixed physical rate, exact two-moment partial-window fibers, and quantified n^-2 instability. Prior Méndez et al. derive the forward renewal law, and Abundo treats inverse first passage at fixed target/rate rather than full moving-target scan. Earlier two-target Resultary theorem varies rate and knows D, and starts at a fixed nonrandom initial site; it does not imply this triple inversion or local equivalence. Literature searches did not locate stronger coverage; absence of discovery is not definitive priority.

Exact all-real-target observations, compact source support, and noiseless physical time scale are essential; no finite-noise minimax guarantee is proved.
